# swarmops cat

Print one file at a revision, or part of it: from a byte, or a range of lines.

```yaml
title: "swarmops cat"
description: "Print one file at a revision, or part of it: from a byte, or a range of lines."
group: "read"
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: false
identity_required: false
mcp_tool: "read_file"
envelope_op: "read_file"
exit_codes: [0, 1, 2, 6]
errors: [E_NOT_A_REPO, E_PATH_NOT_FOUND, E_IS_DIR, E_INVALID_ARG]
syntax: "swarmops cat [OPTIONS] <REV:PATH>"
```

## Syntax

```text
swarmops cat [OPTIONS] <REV:PATH>
```

## Required arguments

### `REV:PATH`

Syntax: `<REV:PATH>`.

The revision and the file's path, split at the first ':'.

## Optional arguments

The command also takes the [global options](../cli.md#global-options).

### `--offset`

Syntax: `--offset <N>`.
Default: `0`.

Start at byte N of the file; a truncated result's next\_offset reads on from there.

### `--lines`

Syntax: `--lines <A-B>`.

Print lines A to B only, numbered from 1, both included, such as 10-20.

### `--max-bytes`

Syntax: `--max-bytes <N>`.
Default: `1048576`.

The most content bytes to print.

## Examples

### CLI

```sh
swarmops --repo [tmp]/store cat main:README.md
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "op": "read_file",
  "api": 1,
  "result": {
    "blob": "[id1]",
    "size": 18,
    "kind": "file",
    "encoding": "utf8",
    "content": "# acme\n\nversion 2\n",
    "truncated": false
  },
  "meta": {
    "repo": "[tmp]/store",
    "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
    "resolved": {
      "main": "[c2]"
    },
    "auth": "trust"
  }
}
```

Exit code 0. Recorded by the CLI tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time.

## Return information

`result` is a `FileContent` (`swarmops schema FileContent` prints its JSON Schema).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `blob` | `string` | yes | The blob's id. |
| `content` | `string` | yes | The bytes returned: those from `offset`, or the requested lines, at most `max_bytes` of them. A cut keeps text as text: it falls where a character starts, so text may stop up to 3 bytes short of `max_bytes`, while bytes that are not text stop at exactly `max_bytes`. |
| `encoding` | `ContentEncoding` | yes | How `content` encodes the bytes it returns: `utf8` when they are text, `base64` when they are not (as when `offset` falls inside a character). |
| `kind` | `FileKind` | yes | The file's kind. |
| `lines` | `LineRange or null` | no | For a request by `lines`: the lines of its range that exist, which `content` holds (the start of them when `truncated`); omitted when none does. |
| `next_offset` | `integer or null` | no | When `truncated`: where `content` stops, the `offset` that reads on from there. A cut text holds whole characters, so a `max_bytes` under 4 can stop before a longer character at the `offset` it started from. |
| `offset` | `integer or null` | no | Where `content` starts in the file, in bytes: the request's `offset`, or where the first of its `lines` that exists starts (the file's size when none does); omitted when that is the file's start. |
| `size` | `integer` | yes | The whole blob's size in bytes, also when `content` is part of it. |
| `truncated` | `boolean` | yes | Whether `content` stops before the end of what was asked for: the file, from `offset`; or the requested lines that exist. |

Envelope `op`: `read_file`.

Exit codes:

- `0`: Success.
- `1`: The operation failed.
- `2`: The request or the command line is malformed.
- `6`: Something the request names does not exist.

## Errors

- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo) (exit 6): No store at the given path, or no store was named.
- [`E_PATH_NOT_FOUND`](../errors.md#e_path_not_found) (exit 6): The path does not exist at that revision.
- [`E_IS_DIR`](../errors.md#e_is_dir) (exit 1): A file operation named a directory.
- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2): A malformed argument or request, including a command-line usage error.

Any command that opens a store may also fail with a store error, such as [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo), [`E_IO`](../errors.md#e_io) or [`E_STORE_CORRUPT`](../errors.md#e_store_corrupt); a command line the grammar refuses is [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2).
